newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt announces no new savings '97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt announces no new savings '97 budget.

text.p: The Swedish government announced no new savings when it tabled its 1997 budget on Friday.
After announcing proposed savings of 22 billion crowns in 1997 and 1998 in an April budget, the government said it saw public sector finances in balance in 1998.
It set a target of reaching a surplus in public finances after 1998.
"The general government financial balance has improved more rapidly than was estimated in the spring bill in April," a statement from the Finance Ministry said.
"Unexpected large tax payments during the first half of 1996 have brought about an upwards revision of tax revenues for 1996."

The ministry said this improvement had been more rapid than foreseen in the state's programme to comply with EU convergence criteria. The assessment of public finances for 1997 and 1998 was substantially in accord with the assessment made in its previous review.

"Allowing for the additional budget reinforcements proposed in the spring fiscal policy bill, the deficit for 1997 is expected to amount to 2.6 percent of GDP which will mean that Sweden will meet the convergence conditions reference value by some margin," the statement said.
"In 1998 the public sector is expected to achieve financial balance."
It said general government financial savings will then have improved by about 10.8 percent of GDP between 1994 and 1998.
"A reduced expenditure ratio accounts for 8.5 percentage units of this improvement and higher revenue in relation to GDP for 2.2 percentage units."
